e: An avalanche hits a base camp near Himlung Himal peak, killing at least four people.
Former chief justice Cholendra Shumsher JB Rana is briefly taken into police custody under unspecified circumstances.
Gauri Kumar Yadav resigns as industry minister amid criticism over her remarks on the liquified petroleum gas bottling sector.
A magnitude 4.9 earthquake hits Gandaki Province, causing extensive damage in Mustang District.
At least 1,451 people are killed following a flash flood along the border with Tibet.
Hindu–Muslim communal riots break out in southern Nepal, leaving at least three people dead.
A Turkish Airlines passenger aircraft catches fire while landing at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu. All passengers and crew are evacuated.
A jeep carrying pilgrims plunges off a cliff in Rolpa District, killing 20 people.
Nepal announces that government and educational institutions will have two days off work during the week instead of one, as part of an effort to save fuel.
Former prime minister K. P. Sharma Oli is arrested over his alleged involvement in the crackdown on the 2025 Nepalese Gen Z protests.
Following his Rastriya Swatantra Party's landslide victory in the general election, Balendra Shah is sworn as Prime Minister of Nepal, succeeding interim prime minister Sushila Karki.
A bus carrying Indian pilgrims falls off a mountain near Shahid Lakhan, killing seven people and injuring nine others.
A vehicle carrying an election team plunges in Ramechhap, killing two people.
A bus falls into the Trishuli River in Dhading District, killing 19 people and injuring 25 others.
A bus falls off a mountain road in Baitadi District, killing 13 people and injuring 34 others.
Six people are arrested as part of an investigation into insurance fraud involving fraudulent helicopter rescues of travellers valued at $19.69 million.
A curfew is declared in Birgunj following protests over the vandalism of a mosque.
An aircraft belonging to Buddha Air overshoots the runway while landing at Bhadrapur Airport from Kathmandu, injuring seven people.
